blocks.why: Full night in your own bed before an easy 10:00 report — bank it, because the next 48 hours are all backside of the clock.
Straight to bed after the BCN turn: this five and a half hours is the only sleep you'll get before an 00:55 report, so blackout blinds and phone off.
Home by 09:25 off the Dublin night — get your head down immediately, before the morning light kills it, because you're back at report at 18:30.
In at 02:35 after the LHR night — sleep as long as your body lets you, first day off is for paying back the debt.
First proper normal night; start walking bedtime backwards now for the 06:10 report on the 7th.
An hour earlier again — the body clock only moves about an hour a day, so do it gradually.
23:00 to 07:00 local, one more step towards an early-start body clock.
Deliberate 21:00 bedtime on your last day off so the 04:20 alarm for a 06:10 report isn't a two-hour night.
Short kip after the Lisbon turn to take the edge off, and still leave you sleepy enough for a 20:30 bedtime.
Early to bed for the 05:40 report — tomorrow is a four-sector 12-hour day and this is all the sleep you get.
Home at 18:45 wrecked after four sectors; long sleep into the day off to clear the debt.
An early-afternoon hour so you can survive being awake until 20:00 and still hit the 04:35 report fresh-ish.
20:00 lights out on a day off — feels wrong, but a 04:35 report means the alarm goes at 02:45.
Nap on landing back from Frankfurt so you're not running on a six-hour night into a normal evening.
Longest night you can get before the 16-hour Stockholm day — this is the sleep that has to carry you to 06:51 tomorrow morning.
Compulsory pre-duty nap: you sign on at 14:40 and don't stop flying until sunrise, so bank two hours before you leave.
Straight to bed at 08:15 off the ARN night — sleep the morning, then get up so you can still sleep tonight for the sim.
Re-anchoring to a normal night ahead of an 08:00 sim start.
Long one after the sim — mentally that's as tiring as a four-sector day.
Normal night; four days off, so the job is to arrive at the 18th with zero sleep debt.
Start creeping bedtime earlier for the 05:05 report on the 18th.
22:00 to 06:00 — one more hour earlier, no lie-in, keep the pressure on.
Short afternoon top-up on the last day off, insurance in case tonight's early bedtime doesn't take.
20:15 bedtime for an 03:15 alarm — the 18th is a 17-hour day and you cannot start it short.
Home just before 23:00 after nearly 17 hours; take everything the clock allows before tomorrow's late finish.
Nap before signing on at 14:40 — you land at 04:13 tomorrow morning and you'll be flying the last sector through the worst hour of the night.
In the door at 05:40, sleep the morning off, then get up around midday so you can still sleep tonight.
Second sleep of the day off, aimed at putting a proper night behind you before another 02:55 finish.
Forty-five minutes before you leave for the 12:20 report — small, but it buys you the last two sectors.
Home at 03:50; sleep until mid-morning only, because tonight has to be an early night for a 04:35 report.
19:30 lights out after only nine hours awake — it will be a fight, but the 23rd is the longest duty of the month.
Nine hours after a 17-hour four-sector day; don't set an alarm any earlier than you have to.
Early night again for the 05:40 CDG report — short day tomorrow, so this is enough.
Nap on the way into three days off, then stay up for a normal bedtime and reset properly.
First full recovery night of the block — no alarm.
Normal night; the last two duties are afternoon reports so you can drift back to civilian hours.
Keep it regular — same time in, same time out.
Late report tomorrow at 15:25, so a normal night with a lie-in is exactly right.
Home around 23:45 from Frankfurt; sleep in, because tomorrow finishes at 03:22.
An hour down before the 13:15 report — the Rome sector lands at 02:52 and that hour is what keeps you sharp for it.
Straight to bed at 02:45 after the last sector of the month — nothing else in the diary, sleep it out.

conflicts.statement: The BCN day duty ends 14:54 local and you report again at 00:55 local — about 10 hours door-to-door, of which the commute takes nearly two, so the only sleep available is an evening nap.
options: Ask crewing to split these two duties across different crew members
Protect a hard 17:00–22:30 local nap and treat the day as a night duty from the moment you land at 14:24
Request the 01/09 BCN turn be dropped so the night duty starts from a rested state

conflicts.statement: MD882/MD826 (report 00:55, off blocks 07:58 local) sits entirely across 02:00–06:00 body time, with no acclimatisation credit and no prior night sleep.
options: Plan controlled rest on the DUB–MAD sector by agreement with the other pilot
Caffeine timed for top of descent inbound MAD, not before
Flag as a fatigue risk to the operator before the pairing

conflicts.statement: You block in from the Dublin night at 07:58 local and report for the LHR duty at 18:30 the same day — roughly 10 hours at home, all of it in daylight, chasing sleep your body clock does not want to give.
options: Ask for the 18:30 LHR duty to be reassigned — this is the single worst pairing in the month
Sleep 10:00–15:30 local in blackout and accept a shortened evening
File a fatigue report if you go, and consider a discretion-free approach on the 01:10 arrival

conflicts.statement: 16h11 duty, four sectors, report 14:40 and off duty 06:51 the next morning — the last sector ARN–MAD flies right through 02:00–06:00 body time at the end of a very long day.
options: Take the pre-duty nap 11:00–13:15 local as non-negotiable
Agree in-seat controlled rest for the ARN sectors
Decline any discretion extension on the final sector

conflicts.statement: The 12th is printed as LIB but you are on duty until 06:51 local that morning, so the day off is really a recovery day and gives you no useful rest credit.
options: Ask the operator whether the 12th counts as a day off under your agreement
Treat it purely as recovery — no personal commitments before mid-afternoon
Request the 13/09 sim be moved later than 08:00 to allow two clean nights

conflicts.statement: Report 06:10 on the 7th then 05:40 on the 8th, and the 8th is a four-sector 12h07 duty — the sleep before it is capped at about seven hours no matter how well you plan it.
options: Go to bed at 20:30 local on the 7th and accept the short afternoon
Use the post-flight nap on the 7th to build a two-sleep day
Ask crewing to swap the 8th for a later report given the sector count

conflicts.statement: 16h56 duty, four sectors, starting from an 05:05 report — the pre-duty sleep has to end at 03:15 local, which realistically means seven hours at best against a seventeen-hour day.
options: Bring bedtime back to 20:15 local across the 15th–17th so the early night is achievable
Plan controlled rest on the ARN sectors
Raise it with the operator as an early start combined with a maximum-length FDP

conflicts.statement: A 14h03 duty finishing at 04:43 local follows the 16h56 duty of the 18th with only about 16h39 between them — two WOCL-crossing days back to back with one short night in the middle.
options: Protect both the 23:15 night sleep and the 11:30 pre-duty nap
Ask for the 19th to be reassigned given the previous day's length
Plan for a fatigue report if the inbound LHR sector runs late

conflicts.statement: You finish at 02:55 local on the 22nd and report at 04:35 local on the 23rd — about 25h40 apart — and the 23rd is a 17h02 four-sector duty, the longest of the month. The single day off cannot absorb that clock swing.
options: Ask crewing for a second day off between the 21st and the 23rd
Split the 22nd into a morning recovery sleep and a 19:30 night sleep as planned, and accept both will be short
Treat the 23rd as a candidate for a fatigue call if either sleep fails

conflicts.statement: 14h07 duty ending 03:22 local on 1 October, following the 29th which finished at 22:48 with about 14h27 rest — and the roster period ends mid-recovery, so nothing after it is visible.
options: Take the pre-duty nap before the 13:15 report
Check what the operator has rostered for 1–2 October before agreeing to the 30th
Agree controlled rest on the FCO–MAD sector

conflicts.statement: The roster prints local time at each station and gives no UTC column, so every instant here is a conversion: MAD/BCN/FRA/CDG/ARN/FCO at UTC+2 and LHR/DUB/LIS at UTC+1 for all of September 2026. The 1h00 report offset and 0h30 post-flight duty end are inferred from the printed columns, not stated in the document.
options: Confirm the report offset with the operator's ops manual before relying on these times
Cross-check one duty against your company app to validate the UTC conversion
If any station's DST assumption is wrong, the affected times shift by one hour
